hypothesis.title: product-catalog memory leak causing OOMKills and 5xx errors
hypothesis.summary: Product-catalog is experiencing a memory leak that began ~26 minutes ago, with heap usage climbing from 36% to over 90% and triggering repeated OOMKills (5 restarts). The OOM crashes cause product-catalog to return "fatal error: runtime: out of memory" errors, which propagate upstream to frontend (9.9% error rate), recommendation, and checkout. The memory growth pattern and unbounded heap usage after full GC strongly indicate a memory leak rather than a transient load spike.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on frontend 5xx errors, but the traces clearly show that 95% of failing frontend traces terminate in product-catalog with "fatal error: runtime: out of memory". Product-catalog itself shows 100% of its failing traces ending internally with the same OOM error. The pod product-catalog-6e17d797-e47e6 has been OOMKilled 5 times and is in a restart loop. Memory utilization metrics show product-catalog jumped from ~36% to ~76% around 25 minutes before the alert, with a peak of 90.9%, and logs confirm "heap usage above 90% after full GC" starting 26 minutes ago. The latency spike in product-catalog (18ms → 84ms p95) and the error spike (0.4% → 7.5%) both align with the memory pressure timeline. Frontend and quote both had deployments 21 minutes before the alert, but frontend's own metrics show stable CPU and memory, and the errors it logs are all downstream failures ("failed calling product-catalog", "failed calling recommendation", "failed calling checkout")—all of which depend on product-catalog. The recommendation service also depends on product-catalog per the call graph, explaining those errors. PostgreSQL metrics are healthy (4ms p95, stable error rate, low CPU), ruling out datastore degradation. The pattern matches PM-2026-05-04 (recommendation OOM from unbounded cache), suggesting a memory leak in product-catalog rather than a transient spike.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Direct evidence of OOMKills: product-catalog pod has been terminated 5 times with OOMKilled reason, confirming memory exhaustion is the failure mechanism.
336 warnings of heap usage above 90% after full GC starting 26 minutes ago indicate the service cannot reclaim memory, a hallmark of a memory leak.
Memory jumped from 36% to 76% (peak 90.9%) around 25 minutes before the alert, showing rapid growth consistent with a leak rather than gradual accumulation.
95% of failing frontend traces terminate in product-catalog, proving product-catalog is the error origin, not just a symptom.
Product-catalog's own traces show internal OOM errors ('fatal error: runtime: out of memory'), confirming the fault is within product-catalog itself.
PostgreSQL latency remains stable at 4ms with no error spike, ruling out datastore degradation as the root cause.

suggested_actions.title: Increase product-catalog memory limit to stop OOMKills
suggested_actions.rationale: Immediately stop the crash loop to restore service. This buys time to investigate the leak without continuous restarts. Current limit is likely too low for the workload or leak rate.

suggested_actions.title: Capture heap dump before next OOM
suggested_actions.command: kubectl -n otel-demo exec -it deploy/product-catalog -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/debug/pprof/heap > product-catalog-heap.prof
suggested_actions.rationale: Collect memory profile to identify which objects/caches are growing unbounded. Essential for root-cause analysis of the leak.

suggested_actions.title: Restart product-catalog deployment to clear leaked memory
suggested_actions.rationale: If increasing memory limit is not sufficient or while waiting for a fix, a restart will clear the leaked memory and restore normal operation temporarily.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Frontend was deployed 21 minutes before the alert (2.0.2 → 2.0.3), but frontend's own CPU and memory are stable, and all its logged errors are downstream failures from product-catalog, recommendation, and checkout. The traces show errors originating in product-catalog, not frontend.
